title: The Exile of El Cid
description: 1081-1094. Banished from Castile by King Alfonso VI, Rodrigo Diaz de Vivar must survive as a mercenary captain: serve the Muslim king of Zaragoza against his rivals, win battles that restore his reputation, and finally conquer Valencia in his own name. The player's small retinue grows through victories; losing El Cid himself means defeat.

issues_found: El Cid himself is placed as a generic CHAMPION even though the engine ships a dedicated 'El Cid' hero unit (used in the official El Cid campaign) — an avoidable substitution, and the defeat trigger fires on the death of an anonymous Champion

Player 1 is assigned FRANKS rather than SPANISH, despite the Spanish civilisation existing and being the obvious fit for a Castilian retinue (Franks give French castle/architecture and Throwing Axemen availability)
Player 2 civilisation is left as RANDOM, so Zaragoza/Barcelona/Valencia architecture (mosque, Middle-Eastern building set) is not guaranteed — the taifa cities may render with any civ's buildings

All three distinct antagonists — al-Mutamin's Zaragoza (ally), Berenguer Ramon II of Barcelona (enemy), and Ibn Jahhaf's Valencia (target) — are collapsed into a single Player 2 roster, so the player's Muslim patron is indistinguishable from his Muslim and Christian enemies

Berenguer Ramon II, named and given dialogue, has no unit representing him; his 'defeat' is a DESTROY_OBJECT on an unnamed KING, so the historically notable capture (not death) of the Count of Barcelona at Tébar is misrepresented as a kill

Force scale is token: a 141-object map with 8 Player 1 units and 12 Player 2 units for a thirteen-year mercenary career and a two-year siege; the two-year starvation siege of Valencia is reduced to breaking one gate
TREE_PALM_FOREST across the map suits coastal Valencia but not the Ebro valley around Zaragoza and Almenar

El Cid is represented by a generic CHAMPION (infantry) even though the engine ships a dedicated El Cid Campeador hero unit (mounted) — an entirely avoidable substitution, and it also misrepresents Rodrigo as a foot soldier rather than the mounted captain of the sources
Player 1 is assigned FRANKS; the Spanish civilization exists in the engine and is the obvious fit for a Castilian exile's retinue (Franks gives Frankish architecture and no Spanish unique units)
Player 2's civilization is left RANDOM, so the architecture and unit set of the taifa/Valencian defenders is unpredictable and may render as anything from Britons to Mongols

Berenguer Ramon II of Barcelona (a Catalan Christian count) and Ibn Jahhaf's Valencia are merged into the single Player 2 slot, whose roster mixes CAMEL_RIDERs and CAVALRY_ARCHERs with the Barcelona coalition — the Christian coalition of Almenar/Tébar is thereby given a Muslim army

Al-Mutamin ibn Hud of Zaragoza, El Cid's employer and a speaking character in the text, has no player slot at all; the only stand-in is a GAIA KING, so the patron-mercenary relationship that defines 1081-1090 is not actually playable
Berenguer Ramon II was historically captured, not killed, at Tébar; the trigger 'Barcelona Defeated' fires on DESTROY_OBJECT, so play kills a man the narration correctly says was taken alive
Ibn Jahhaf's death is placed at the moment of the city's fall in 1094; he was in fact executed some months afterward
